description:
You are born into a family of silk weavers in Constantinople, not long after monks first smuggled the secret of silk out of China for an emperor who refused to keep paying Persia's price for it. From a girl learning her first thread to a master weaver trusted with a king's gift, live a whole quiet life spent at the loom, through one color you may never wear and one night the whole city nearly burns.

This is a slow, sensory bedtime history told in the second person, for falling asleep to: rain on courtyard tiles, lamplight on silk thread, and a craft passed from mother to daughter across an entire lifetime.
era_setting: Constantinople, the Byzantine Empire, roughly the 530s-580s CE: narrow lamplit workshop streets, brick courtyard houses, the Hippodrome and the Golden Horn's docks, undyed linen and wool clothing with rare glimpses of forbidden imperial purple silk.

scenes.narration: You are born into a family that has woven silk for generations, in a city built on one stolen secret.
Two monks once smuggled silkworms out of China, hidden inside a hollow walking cane.
By twelve, you can weave a plain bolt alone, checked thread by thread under lamplight.
Then one market day, you see a color no ordinary hand is allowed to touch.
It is Tyrian purple, worth more than its own weight in gold, reserved for the emperor alone.
Even dyeing it without leave, your mother warns, is treated as a kind of theft.
Years later, a foreign king's envoy lifts your own silk to the light, and says nothing at all.

shorts.title: The Night Constantinople Nearly Burned #shorts
shorts.description: A chariot-race chant turned into the riot that almost ended the Byzantine Empire. This is what it looked like from one rooftop. #history #constantinople #shorts

scenes.narration: At twenty, you know the Hippodrome only as noise, color, and cheering crowds.
One afternoon, those same crowds turn into a single furious mob within the hour.
They chant one word, nika, meaning victory, but no one in this city wins today.
From your rooftop, you watch flame climb toward the church you were christened in.
Your husband carries your family's silk into the cistern room, hoping water can save it.
For three nights you listen to a city you love tear itself apart outside.
When it ends, half of Constantinople lies blackened, and nothing here will be the same again.
